name: BOHB
tagline: Hyperband bracket scheduler whose configuration sampler is replaced with a TPE KDE model on all completed trials.
pseudocode:
1. Initialize $s_{\max} = \lfloor \log_\eta(\text{budget}) \rfloor$ Hyperband brackets ($\eta = 3$)
2. For each bracket sample its $n$ initial configs from a TPE model: l(x)/g(x) using $\gamma=0.15$ split
3. Run successive halving inside each bracket: keep top $1/\eta$, multiply fidelity by $\eta$
4. After every observed (config, score, fidelity), append to the global TPE history
5. When all bracket queues empty, propose new configs from the TPE model at fidelity $1.0$

key_hyperparams.name: gamma
key_hyperparams.role: fraction kept as 'good' for TPE KDE

key_hyperparams.name: n_startup
key_hyperparams.role: random configs before TPE kicks in

diff_from_baseline: Falkner, Klein & Hutter 2018 (BOHB, ICML). Combines Hyperband's multi-fidelity successive halving with TPE-style KDE-based config sampling, using all observed (config, fidelity) trials to bias future proposals.

name: DEHB
tagline: Differential Evolution operates on per-fidelity populations; Hyperband promotes top configs to higher fidelities.
pseudocode:
1. Build deduplicated fidelity ladder $\{1/\eta^s\}_{s\le 3}$ with floor 0.1; initialise random pop per fidelity
2. For each new (config, score), match to the pending DE trial and run DE selection: keep better of target/trial
3. When the lowest fidelity finishes a generation, evolve via DE/rand/1/bin: $v = x_a + F(x_b - x_c)$, crossover with prob $C_r$
4. Every $\eta$ generations, promote top $1/\eta$ of a fidelity to the next; their populations replace the higher-fidelity pop
5. Loop until budget exhausted; fall back to random at full fidelity if queue empties
diff_from_baseline: Awad, Mallik & Hutter 2021 (DEHB, IJCAI). Multi-fidelity hyperparameter optimizer that replaces Hyperband's random sampling with Differential Evolution evolving distinct populations per fidelity, with cross-fidelity SH promotion.

name: Hyperband
tagline: Bandit-based multi-fidelity scheduler running successive halving over an outer grid of (n configs, budget per config).
pseudocode:
1. $s_{\max} = \lfloor \log_\eta(\text{budget})\rfloor$, capped at 4
2. For each bracket $s = s_{\max} \ldots 0$:
3.   $n = \lceil (s_{\max}+1)/(s+1) \rceil \eta^s$ random configs at fidelity $r = \max(1/\eta^s, 0.1)$
4. After each round, advance bracket by SH: keep top $\lfloor n/\eta \rfloor$, multiply fidelity by $\eta$ (capped at 1.0)
5. Pop one (config, fidelity) per call; fall back to uniform random when queue is empty
diff_from_baseline: Li, Jamieson, DeSalvo, Rostamizadeh & Talwalkar 2017 (Hyperband, JMLR). Multi-fidelity HPO that runs successive halving inside several outer brackets trading off n vs r; non-model-based but adapts resource allocation to performance.

name: CMA-ES (Optuna-style)
tagline: (mu/mu_w, lambda)-CMA-ES on the unit-cube encoding: adapts the full covariance and step size with rank-one and rank-mu updates.
pseudocode:
1. Encode each parameter to $[0,1]$ (log/categorical-aware), set $\mathbf{m}=0.5\mathbf{1}$, $C=I$, $\sigma=0.3$, $\lambda = 4 + \lfloor 3\ln d\rfloor$, $\mu = \lfloor\lambda/2\rfloor$
2. Sample $\lambda$ candidates: $x_i = \mathbf{m} + \sigma\, C^{1/2} z_i,\; z_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0,I)$, clipped to $[0,1]$
3. After all $\lambda$ scored, sort descending; recompute mean as weighted avg of top $\mu$
4. Update evolution paths $p_\sigma, p_c$ with cumulation constants $c_\sigma, c_c$
5. Update $C$ via rank-one ($p_c p_c^\top$) and rank-$\mu$ (weighted outer products of normalized differences)
6. Update step size $\sigma \leftarrow \sigma \exp((c_\sigma/d_\sigma)(\|p_\sigma\|/\chi_n - 1))$, then resample
diff_from_baseline: Hansen & Ostermeier 2001 (CMA-ES); also Nomura et al. 2021 (warm-start CMA-ES). Standard $(\mu/\mu_w,\lambda)$-CMA-ES on the encoded unit cube with rank-one + rank-$\mu$ covariance updates and CSA step-size control, matching Optuna's CmaEsSampler.

name: Random Search
tagline: Sample each suggestion uniformly at random from the typed search space; ignore history.
diff_from_baseline: Bergstra & Bengio 2012 (JMLR). Sample configurations uniformly from the typed space ignoring history; surprisingly strong baseline on high-dim spaces with low effective dimensionality.

name: TPE
tagline: Tree-structured Parzen Estimator: split history into good/bad by the top-gamma quantile and pick candidates maximizing log l(x) - log g(x).
pseudocode:
1. While $|\text{history}| < n_{\text{startup}} = 10$, sample uniformly
2. Encode each observed config to $[0,1]^d$ (log-aware for log_scale params; index/(K-1) for categoricals)
3. Threshold $y^*$ at the top-$\gamma$ quantile; build Gaussian KDEs $l, g$ over good/bad sets
4. Bandwidth $\sigma = \max(0.05,\, \mathrm{std}(\text{set}) + \epsilon)$ (Scott's rule proxy)
5. Sample 24 random candidates and pick the one maximizing $\log l(x) - \log g(x)$; return at fidelity 1.0

key_hyperparams.name: gamma
key_hyperparams.role: fraction of best obs assigned to l(x)

diff_from_baseline: Bergstra, Bardenet, Bengio & Kegl 2011 (NeurIPS). Models p(x|y<y*) and p(x|y>=y*) via KDEs and proposes candidates maximizing l(x)/g(x), equivalent to maximizing Expected Improvement under TPE's modeling assumptions.
